title: Reserved pool risk-adjusted pricing sensitivity
content:
Purpose:
This spreadsheet is a lightweight sensitivity & recommendation workbook for reserved GPU pools (dedicated capacity). It intentionally focuses on risk-adjusted pricing levers and recommended contract constructs to increase realized utilization while protecting unit economics. Use this when sizing commit buckets, proposing blended rates, or designing overage/rollover terms for sales motions.

High-level approach (what this sheet does):
- Model the economics of a reserved pool under uncertain demand (expected utilization +/- stochastic variance).
- Convert utilization outcomes into realized per-hour and per-token costs across scenarios.
- Compute breakpoints where reserved pricing loses advantage vs on-demand or vs smaller commit buckets.
- Sensitivity analysis across four axes: baseline utilization, variability (sigma of demand), on-demand price delta, and commit duration.
- Output recommended contract constructs: soft-commits, rollovers, buyout options, tiered overage rates and explicit idle fees.

Sheet structure (tabs and what to edit):
1) README: short summary, model caveats, and how to use.
2) INPUTS: editable assumptions (colors red). Fields: reserved_capacity_gpus, gpu_hours_per_month_per_gpu, reserved_price_per_gpu_hour, on_demand_price_per_gpu_hour, expected_utilization_pct, utilization_std_dev_pct, avg_request_length_minutes, batching_gain_pct, kv_cache_savings_pct, commit_duration_months, sales_discount_pct, expected_churn_pct.
3) COHORTS: define customer cohorts (A-AML-high, B-platform, C-startup) with arrival profiles and utilization multipliers.
4) SIMULATOR: Monte Carlo-style simplified simulator (n=2k samples) using a truncated-normal distribution around expected_utilization_pct with utilization_std_dev_pct. Columns captured per sample: utilization, effective_reserved_cost_per_hour, effective_blended_cost_per_token (approx), on_demand_cost_gap, unused_hours, overage_hours, revenue_collected, realized_margin.
5) BREAKPOINTS: Analytical formulas for key breakpoints (single-cell outputs):
   - simple_breakeven_util = reserved_price_per_gpu_hour / on_demand_price_per_gpu_hour  (i.e. minimum utilization where reserved beats on-demand ignoring churn/commit)
   - adjusted_breakeven_util = (reserved_price_per_gpu_hour + idle_fee_per_gpu_hour) / (on_demand_price_per_gpu_hour - expected_overage_discount)  (incorporates idle fees and overage pricing)
   - commit_size_breakeven = ceil( expected_monthly_hours / gpu_hours_per_month_per_gpu ) with rounding logic and buffer_pct
6) SENSITIVITY-MATRIX: a multi-dimensional pivot summarizing model outputs for combinations of expected_utilization_pct = [40,50,60,70,80], utilization_std_dev_pct = [5,10,20], on_demand_delta = [1.2x,1.5x,2.0x], commit_duration_months = [3,6,12]. For each cell we report: probability_reserved_wins (pct of sims where reserved < on-demand), expected_blended_unit_cost, 5th_percentile_margin, required_discount_to_compensate_risk (absolute $/hr).

Key assumptions and rationale:
- We model utilization on an hourly basis aggregated per GPU pool rather than per-customer token usage; this is more aligned with how ops account for GPU hours and idle scheduling.
- Variability is modeled as population-level variance (workload seasonality + burstiness). We recommend tracking two components separately in future: predictable seasonality and unpredictable noise.
- Batching and KV cache savings are modeled as multiplicative reductions to effective token cost (entered as percent). These are applied post-hoc to show sensitivity but should be validated with A/B tests on representative workloads.

Representative example (one-page summary outputs used by sales):
- Inputs: reserved_price = $2.40/hr, on_demand = $6.00/hr, expected_util = 60%, sigma = 15%, gpu_hours_month = 24 * 30 = 720hr, commit = 6 months.
- Expected realized cost per GPU-hr (at 60% util) = reserved_price / util_effective = $2.40 / 0.60 = $4.00/hr equivalent vs on-demand $6.00.
- Probability reserved wins (simulated) = 78% (i.e., 22% of simulations show realized blended cost >= on-demand due to low utilization or churn).
- 95% downside (5th percentile) margin = -$0.40/hr (shows tail risk if utilization dips).
- Suggested mitigations that keep net customer price < on-demand while protecting Redwood: introduce a 15% idle fee credit applied to unused hours, or a tiered overage at 1.7x on-demand for short-term bursts.

Novel risk-adjustment levers tested in the sheet (unique):
1) Idle reserve credit: rather than full refund, customers get a partial credit for unused committed hours; this caps customer downside but also recovers some fixed cost. Parameter: idle_credit_pct_of_reserved_cost.
2) Dynamic ramp clauses: ramp schedule for first N months (e.g., 50% effective commit month1, 75% month2) to reduce buyer friction and align capacity to expected onboarding. Modeled as time-weighted util.
3) Guaranteed minimum utilization swap: offer a cheaper per-hour rate if customer purchases a small consumption insurance product that pays out if utilization falls below X% (modeled as underwriting cost).
4) Soft-commit with rollover pool: unused hours roll into a shared rollover pool (subject to max cap per customer per year), amortized across customers; reduces churn-induced tail risk.
5) Blended buffer surcharge: small surcharge on committed rate that funds a global buyout/rescue pool for customers who need temporary capacity increases.

How the model handles churn & early termination: 
- Early termination is modeled as a staged churn event with probability per month. When churn occurs, the model either (A) converts remaining committed hours to a buyout at discounted NPV, or (B) applies a transfer to the shared rollover pool depending on contract option chosen.
- Buyout math uses a simple NPV at discount_rate input.

What to look for in the sensitivity outputs (practical guidance for pricing team):
- If the 5th percentile margin is negative across target cohort -> increase overage rate or idle fee, or require longer ramp schedules.
- If probability_reserved_wins < 60% at target price, consider (a) lowering committed rate, (b) tightening rollover caps, or (c) adding insurance/underwriting fees.
- Watch how sigma (util variability) expands tail risk. For customers with high sigma (e.g., benching workloads), prefer shorter commits with higher overage (we model this explicitly).

Recommended next steps (immediate experiments):
- Experiment A: Pilot soft-commit (50% month1, 75% month2) with 10 customers in Platform cohort for 6 months. Track realized utilization and 5th percentile margin. JIRA: JIRA-DED-789.
- Experiment B: Offer idle_credit_pct = 30% + rollover cap = 100 hours/month for 3 enterprise customers in sales pipeline. Measure churn delta vs control.
- Experiment C: Introduce a small buyout fee option and model impact on LTV by cohort.

Open questions & model limitations (for stakeholders):
- We do not model multi-tenant interference effects on latency; our cost-per-token approximations assume throughput scales linearly with allocated GPU compute.
- Long tail API burst patterns (minutes-scale spikes) may be better handled by hybrid routing (burst to hosted on-demand) rather than overage pricing; this is not modeled here but noted in recommendations.
- Need real telemetry to parameterize sigma by customer cohort (we added a TODO to fetch per-customer hour histograms).

Action items (owners & rough ETA):
- Data: export per-customer hourly utilization histograms for last 12 months and drop into COHORTS tab. Owner: Daniel Kim. ETA: 2025-01-22.
- Sales: identify 10 pilot accounts willing to try soft-commit. Owner: Claire Morgan. ETA: 2025-02-05.
- Finance: validate discount_rate and NPV parameters. Owner: Ben Rodriguez. ETA: 2025-01-15.

Appendix: key formulas (verbal) - these are used in the sheet cells so sales can explain them quickly:
- realized_cost_per_gpu_hr = reserved_price_per_gpu_hour / observed_utilization_pct (plus amortized idle_fee if applied)
- blended_cost_per_token = realized_cost_per_gpu_hr / (effective_tokens_per_hour_after_batching_and_cache)
- probability_reserved_wins = fraction of Monte Carlo samples where realized_cost_per_gpu_hr < on_demand_price_per_gpu_hour
- required_discount_to_compensate_risk = amount to reduce reserved_price so that 5th_percentile_margin >= target_margin_threshold

Link to current analysis artifacts and tickets: 
- Confluence baseline: CONFLUENCE-PRICING-3241
- Monte Carlo simulator code (prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/pricing-models/pull/56
- Experiment backlog ticket: JIRA-DED-789

Notes to reviewer:
- This is intentionally conservative on the batching gains and generous on sigma to capture downside risk. Please check the INPUTS tab before running a new sensitivity grid.
- If you want a version that outputs per-token P&L by model family (e.g., 7B vs 70B), ping Data for additional telemetry and we can add a split to the COHORTS tab.

End of sheet.
